chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Prayer is disliked in three places on the road: Al-Bayda', which is Dhat al-Jaysh, and Dhat al-Salaasil, and Dajnan.
He said, and he said: There is no harm in praying between the back roads, which are the avenues (Jawadd) of the road; and it is disliked to pray in the avenue.
ai.seo_question: Where is prayer disliked on the road according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details specific geographical spots along roads where prayer is disliked (makruh), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on environmental purity and avoiding places associated with impurity or social disruption. While it explicitly prohibits prayer in three named locations—Al-Bayda', Dhat al-Jaysh, and Dhat al-Salaasil—it distinguishes the 'Jawadd' (back roads/avenues) as permissible yet still carrying a degree of dislike, highlighting the nuanced juristic approach to spatial sanctity in ritual practice.
